title: The ride and the recall
topic: Waymo opens San Antonio robotaxi rides to anyone with the app, the airport included, while the federal recall about driving into standing water still lists its remedy as under development
credits:

SOURCES
Waymo, October 14th
NHTSA recall 26E026
Texas Public Radio, May 10th and 13th

scenes.vo: Anyone in San Antonio can now hail a Waymo with no driver, the airport included.

requests.purpose: Carry one white driverless car through the film so the viewer follows it arriving at the airport curb, sitting empty in a creek crossing and a street flood, slowing into standing water on a lane and waiting at the curb again, with every state it reaches kept for the rest of the film.
requests.prompt: Author an original finished React and SVG object in the current Remotion engine. A long rounded white sport utility robotaxi with a roof sensor pod, small side sensors, dark glass that shows an empty driver seat and a steering wheel, black wheel arches, visible rims, lit headlamps, brake lamps and amber hazard lamps, a scuffed lower door, a mud line that rises after water, and a rear door that opens. Late sodium light from the upper left, cool fill from the right, a long soft shadow. No logos, no brand marks and no real model badge. Maintained but worn, nothing symmetric. A disclosed illustration, never a real vehicle.
requests.source_limit: Disclosed illustration of a generic white driverless car. Not a Waymo vehicle, a vehicle in the recall, a real road, speed, depth or rider.

requests.purpose: Give the car a believable world: the airport pickup curb and phone request, the street map with its outlined area, the creek and low crossing, the flooded street, the higher speed lane with standing water, and the recall record cards, counter grid, stamps, calendar and fleet row.
requests.prompt: Author an original finished React and SVG support group in the current Remotion engine. A San Antonio airport pickup curb with a leaning bay sign, bench and concrete texture, a worn phone with a ride request pin, a flat street map with a river line and an outlined area, Salado Creek with a limestone bank and a low crossing with a depth post, a flooded residential street, a higher speed lane with standing water, a desk with a federal recall record card, a grid of small car icons, rubber stamps, a calendar page and a row of cars taking check marks. Maintained but worn, nothing symmetric, warm concrete and storm slate palette, no real brand marks. A disclosed illustration.
requests.source_limit: Disclosed illustration. Not a real airport, creek, street, lane, record page or app screen, and it draws no real rider or property.

film_direction.angle: Hold the same white car as a roof pod and a record card from above, so the viewer reads the ride and the recall as two entries on one page.
film_direction.opening_promise: Watch one driverless car take a ride, then see what the federal record says about water on the road.
film_direction.performed_turn: The car slows and then rolls on into standing water across the lane, exactly as the recall sentence words it, and no stop is drawn.
film_direction.closing_answer: The airport ride is open to everyone, and the federal record still lists the flood remedy as under development.

story_contract.opening_question: Anyone in San Antonio can now hail a driverless Waymo to the airport. What does the federal record say about the flood problem its recall covers?
story_contract.actor: Waymo, with a recall record held by the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration
story_contract.action: Opened its San Antonio robotaxi rides to anyone with the app, airport included, after filing a software recall about driving into standing water.
story_contract.change: Driverless rides in San Antonio move from invited riders in a limited area to anyone with the app, while the recall remedy is still listed as under development.
story_contract.affected_people: People who can now hail a ride, airport travelers among them. The April cars were empty and no one was injured, and no rider is named.
story_contract.consequence: A federal record that still lists the flood remedy as under development, beside an interim step of tighter weather limits by April 20th.
story_contract.source_limit: The recall wording is one sentence with no cause, speed or depth. The record does not say what the weather limits are or whether they apply now, and the recall notice itself was not retrieved.
story_contract.closing_answer: The airport ride is open, and the federal record still lists the flood remedy as under development.

throughline.subject: One white driverless car that takes a ride at the airport curb and meets standing water on a lane
throughline.opening_state: A white car glides to the airport curb and the phone says arriving, with nobody at the wheel.
throughline.closing_state: Back at the airport curb the same white car waits with its door open beside a recall record card whose remedy row is marked under development, and the frame holds on that pair.

cinematic_contract.button: The car slows and rolls on into the water, and the close sets the open airport ride beside a remedy row still marked under development.

cinema.visible_action: A white car on a higher speed lane slows and then rolls on into standing water, and the recall record beside it lists the remedy as under development.
cinema.human_consequence: People who can now hail a ride, airport travelers among them, share the road with a recall whose remedy is still under development. The April cars were empty and no one was injured.
cinema.source_limit: Disclosed illustration of the recall wording and Texas Public Radio accounts. It shows no real road, speed, depth or rider, and the record does not say what the weather limits are or whether they apply now.

divergence_note: B reads the same story from above and from inside the cab: roof pods on a plan of the curb, the map, the creek and the lane, a grid of icons that fills, record cards laid flat and details of the empty steering wheel, the cabin and the hazard lamps, and it closes from above on the same bay with the record card sliding in. It trades the ground-level traverse of A for a ledger of plans and details.

creative_direction.viewer_question: Anyone in San Antonio can now hail a driverless Waymo to the airport. What does the federal record say about the flood problem its recall covers?
creative_direction.visible_answer: The airport ride is open and the federal record still lists the flood remedy as under development, shown as a car and a record card held side by side at the same curb.
creative_direction.emotional_turn: Plain curiosity at the curb, unease as the water takes empty cars, and then an even, unhurried answer about what is still unfinished.
creative_direction.medium_choice: News report / Explanatory animation, evidence-led ordering from above. visual_research.decision: No external photograph or footage helps tell this story honestly, so fresh authored illustration performs the sourced events with an Illustration disclosure and no brand marks.

art_direction.palette_reason: Airport concrete and warm sodium haze carry the curb, floodwater is a muddy tan-brown, slate storm gray holds the creek scenes, warm paper carries the record cards, the white of the car is the one clean value, and a single amber is kept only for hazard lamps, stamps and the highlighted may.
art_direction.shape_language: A softly rounded white car body against hard rectangular concrete, the long straight lane marks and flat paper cards with worn corners. Water edges are loose and hand cut. Nothing is symmetric: the bay sign leans, the stamp lands crooked.

lighting.motivation: Low sodium airport light from the upper left warms concrete and the white body, cool storm fill from the right shades the water scenes, and every grounded thing throws a soft shadow to the right.

hero.silhouette: A long rounded white sport utility body with a roof sensor pod, black wheel arches and a glass cabin that shows an empty driver seat.
hero.finish: Lit upper-left painted panels with a soft highlight, cool shaded right side, a scuffed lower door, a mud line after the water, lit brake and hazard lamps, visible wheel rims and a long soft ground shadow.

art_direction.focal_hierarchy: The white car first, the water or the record card second, the phone and the tags third, the street and the sky last.
art_direction.motion_language: The car glides and brakes with continuous acceleration, water rises at an even speed, cards slide and settle without bounce, stamps land once, and the camera holds while objects perform.

signature_shot.reason: The car slows and rolls on into the standing water while the word may lights on the recall sentence, the whole mechanism in one movement.

captions.text: Anyone in San Antonio can now hail a Waymo with no driver,
in a limited area of sixty square miles.
In April, an empty Waymo was swept into Salado Creek.
Earlier that month, another empty car was stranded in floodwater.
that could affect nearly thirty eight hundred cars.
The recall says the software may let a car slow,
then drive into standing water on higher speed roads.
The federal record says the remedy is currently under development.
As an interim step, Waymo tightened its weather limits,
and every affected car had the update by April twentieth.
So the airport ride is open,
and the federal record lists the flood remedy
